clue.text: Applied the Spanish stamp

parts.note: APP is the dictionary abbreviation for applied
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A clerk in Spain sticks a postage stamp on a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: In fencing an APPEL is a stamp of the front foot made to unsettle an opponent; the surface wants a postage stamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Fencers call the sharp tap of the leading foot on the floor by this French term, a feint meant to distract.

clue.text: Turkish officer gets head down — note, one sees this under fire

indicators.note: the officer's opening letter is pushed lower down the word, so the order of his letters changes

parts.note: a pasha was a high-ranking Ottoman officer
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: A Turkish officer ducks under enemy fire.
explanation.walkthrough: PASHA has its first letter moved down to fourth place, giving ASHPA; add N. The surface's 'under fire' is a battle, but the definition means beneath a grate.
explanation.definitionFit: The tray beneath a grate or furnace catches the cinders, so it sits directly below the burning coals.

clue.text: With a proposition MP, sailor and I act improperly

indicators.note: acting improperly means behaving out of order, so these letters are put out of their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician and a seaman behave badly after making an indecent proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's proposition is an improper suggestion; the definition's is a mathematical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A porism is a kind of geometrical proposition in Greek mathematics, and this adjective describes something relating to such a statement.

clue.text: Church breaking up sole organ

indicators.note: the church splits the other word apart by breaking into its middle

parts.note: planta is the anatomical name for the sole of the foot
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church congregation splits up over its only organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' reads as only and 'organ' as the church instrument; sole is the underside of the foot, and organ is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The temporary organ that nourishes a foetus in the womb is a body part, like heart or liver.

clue.text: English prison inmate that is beginning on library book

parts.note: the first letter of library

explanation.surface: An English convict starts reading a library book in his cell.
explanation.walkthrough: A zek is a Gulag prisoner, a word familiar from Solzhenitsyn.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezekiel is one of the prophetic books of the Old Testament, named after the prophet it records.

clue.text: Like mole-ridden land, something of little value, not the first

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a cheapy is an inexpensive, worthless thing

explanation.surface: A field riddled with molehills is worth very little.
explanation.definitionFit: Land dug by moles is covered in small mounds of earth, so it is full of heaps.

clue.text: Green stone since found in Poland and Morocco

parts.note: PL is the international code for Poland
as can mean since, as in 'as it rained'

explanation.definitionFit: Plasma is also a bright green variety of chalcedony, a semi-precious quartz used in jewellery.

clue.text: Rib, one found in ancient swamp

clue.text: Time to score bye that's bowled in the middle over

explanation.walkthrough: Bye, bowled and over all sound like cricket, but bye is a farewell and over is the reversal signal. AT BAT is a baseball term.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball a batter's turn at the plate, the chance to hit and score runs, is called this.

clue.text: Those living on the hills poach my game terribly around river

indicators.note: around means one letter is surrounded by the rearranged others
done terribly means done in a mess, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Hill people complain that poachers are taking their game near the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The hills are anthills, not mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the genus of the giant anteater, animals that feed on ants and so live off anthills.

clue.text: Volume of old bulk carrier offloading tons

indicators.note: offloading means unloading something, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: a tanker is a ship carrying liquid in bulk

explanation.definitionFit: An anker was a historical liquid measure for wine and spirits, about ten gallons, used in northern Europe.

clue.text: Note chicken covered in spots finally healthy in Russian pen

indicators.note: something covered in another thing lies inside it

parts.note: zits are pimples

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of each of the next two words

clue.text: Bird seen around great British tree

clue.text: Scots porter about to stop working

a machine that dies stops working

clue.text: Particular photograph with Luing cattle

clue.text: Cut about a centimetre part off the peak

parts.note: to pare is to trim or cut
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Paracme is the period of decline after the highest point, the stage that falls away once the acme has passed.

clue.text: Form of existence like God's without origin

clue.text: Spineless insurgent that's caught replacing nation's leader

indicators.note: replacing means one letter is swapped in where another stood

parts.note: mutinous means rebellious

parts.note: the first letter of nation

explanation.walkthrough: Spineless is a botanical sense here: lacking points, not cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany a muticous plant or part has no awn or point, so it is blunt and without prickles.

clue.text: Hand in one's kitbag

parts.note: inside the letters of these words

clue.text: Old royal makes active king when mother's gone

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: What's drawn out duet composed around common time

clue.text: To some extent neglecting runs, rarely in a fit way

parts.note: partly means to some extent

explanation.surface: A batsman skips runs and only rarely looks in good form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rarely' tags the answer as an uncommon word; it is part of the definition, not a time word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pat means apt or timely, so the adverb means suitably or aptly.

clue.text: Unsupported rise for rally driver that is former professional youngster

taken as written
